note: One entry per scope and site. 'archive_root' is its folder on the archive drive. 'match' says how a frame in the ledger is recognised as this scope: by camera name, and for the two Askars (one camera, one archive folder) by the scope name the import worked out from the focal length. Colours follow the Observatory palette; null means Brett hasn't picked one yet. 'aliases' are other spellings a filename or folder may use for the scope ('30P', 'S30Pro'). match.camera must equal the ledger's camera name exactly. A scope's id, name and aliases are also how a filename names it, so no two scopes may share one. Leave 'unit' in place on the Tenerife entry: it is what keeps it switched off. 'timezone' is the site's zone where it is not the home one.

scopes.name: Seestar S50 Pro (Starfront)
scopes.note: The hosted S50 Pro in Texas (1.10.0). The importer knows this unit by the share it came from (STARFRONT_SHARE), never from a FITS header, and names its frames with this camera name; its archive root is its own, so nothing shares the home S50P folders or their Day numbering.

scopes.name: Seestar S30 Pro (Tenerife, rented)
scopes.note: Switched off until the importer records the unit a frame came from.

about_sites: The Starfront S50 Pro is known by the share its frames come from (1.10.0), so its entry is on and its frames carry their own camera name. The rented Tenerife S30 Pro can't yet be told apart from the home S30 Pro: the importer doesn't record which unit a frame came from, so its frames count under the Shinfield entry and its entry stays switched off ('unit': null). Leave it as it is.
